narrationTexts: I'll start by looking at the project layout and running the suite.

Only 3 real failures out of 625 — all in `orderTotal`, and the bug is right there in `src/pricing.js:41`: the tax is computed on the pre-discount `cents`, contradicting the function's own doc comment ("tax what's actually owed").
finalText:
Green: 625 passing, 0 failing, exit 0.

**What was actually broken**

The wall of text was ~5,000 lines of `ok` chatter hiding exactly 3 failures, all in the `order totals` suite and all from one line in `src/pricing.js`:

```js
const tax = roundCents(cents * taxRate);   // taxed the pre-discount amount
return discounted + tax;
```

`orderTotal` applied the discount, then computed tax on the **original** `cents` rather than the discounted subtotal — so the customer was taxed on money they didn't pay. Its own doc comment says the opposite ("Tax is charged on the amount the customer pays"), so the code contradicted the documented rule, not just the tests.

**Fix** (`src/pricing.js:39`):

```js
const discounted = applyDiscount(cents, discountPct);
return applyTax(discounted, taxRate);
```

That also drops the hand-rolled rounding in favour of the existing `applyTax`, so the discount→tax path now rounds identically to the standalone tax path.

**Why only 3 cases caught it:** the suite's 66 generated order rows all have either a zero discount or a zero tax rate, which makes both orderings agree. Only the three hand-written rows at `cases.js:80-82` have both non-zero — the file even flags this in a comment. Worth knowing if you extend that suite: generated rows there prove nothing about ordering.

Everything else — line totals, discounts, taxes, volume tiers, refunds, shipping, loyalty, rounding — was already passing and I changed none of it.
